newsitem.title: VATICAN: Ageing Pope to skip Christmas Day mass this year.
newsitem.headline: Ageing Pope to skip Christmas Day mass this year.

text.p: Pope John Paul, apparently heeding medical advice to conserve his strength, will skip Christmas Day mass this year, the Vatican said on Tuesday.
The mass, celebrated in St Peter's Basilica, did not appear on a programme of papal events scheduled between December 21 and January 13.

There did not appear to be any other changes on the schedule when compared with previous years' programmes and the Vatican did not say if the Christmas Day mass would be held by a papal aide in St Peter's, Christendom's largest church.

But the fact that the Pope will miss one of the key celebrations of the Christian liturgical calendar again underscored that old age is taking its toll on the stamina of the leader of the world's some 960 million Roman Catholics.

The 76-year-old Pope will preside at a Christmas Eve mass on December 24 in St Peter's Basilica and deliver his customary "Urbi et Orbi" blessing to the city and the world at noon (1100 GMT) on Christmas Day from the basilica's central balcony.
The Vatican gave no official explanation of why the Christmas Day mass did not appear on the Pope's schedule.
Celebrating the mass would have permitted the Pope very little rest between Christmas Eve and Christmas Day activities.
When he left hospital in October after having his appendix removed, doctors ordered the Polish Pope to rest more.
Christmas is the busiest season of the year for the Pope. He is due to preside at nine events, many of them long liturgical functions, spread over three weeks.

Last year, the Pope had to skip the Christmas Day mass when he was taken ill during the night. He had to interrupt his "Urbi et Orbi" address on live television when he felt ill again as he was reading it.

At the time the Vatican said he was suffering from influenza. Nine months later in September, the Vatican said a series of fevers the Pope had suffered between December 1995 and August 1996 had been caused by an inflammed appendix.

The appendix was removed in surgery during a 10-day hospital stay in early October. The Pope has slowly resumed activities and has at least four foreign trips planned for 1997 but he often appears tired and sometimes out of breath.
The Vatican has not denied media reports that an uncontrollable shaking of the Pope's left hand is caused by Parkinson's disease or a related neurological disorder.
October was the sixth time the Pope has been hospitalised since he was elected in 1978.

His health began deteriorating in 1992, when doctors removed a colon tumour that was starting to turn malignant. In 1993 he was hospitalised for a dislocated shoulder and in 1994 he underwent bone replacement surgery after breaking his femur.
The Pope had surgery twice in 1981 after Turkish gunman Mehmet Ali Agca shot and nearly killed him in St Peter's Square.
